hero.headline: North Palm Beach Celebrates Fourth of July with Fireworks and Pool Party at Country Club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this year's event also recognizes America's 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida advances ban on undocumented students at state colleges as Byron Donalds leads GOP governor's race
cards.body:
Florida's State Board of Education voted this week to advance rules that would prevent undocumented students from enrolling in the state's 28 public colleges and adult education programs, including GED preparation courses. The action follows a separate decision by the state university system's Board of Governors to advance a plan barring undocumented students from Florida's public universities starting in the 2027-28 academic year. Students already enrolled would not be affected by the university proposal.

Supporters of the restrictions contend that taxpayer-funded institutions should prioritize students who are lawfully present in the United States. However, immigrant advocates and students have opposed the rules, arguing they would close educational doors for young people who grew up in Florida and graduated from Florida high schools. Alexander Vallejos, a student Dreamer, said "We're just asking for an opportunity to earn our future through education. Because when Dreamers succeed, Florida succeeds." The restrictions come after Florida previously eliminated in-state tuition rates for many undocumented students, including those protected under DACA.

The education restrictions emerged during a dominant week in Florida's Republican governor's race. Byron Donalds entered the week as the front-runner to succeed term-limited Governor Ron DeSantis. His campaign and affiliated political committee report raising more than 90 million dollars this cycle, including more than 23 million in the second quarter. The campaign recently launched a 20 million dollar statewide advertising buy. Donalds also received endorsements from Attorney General James Uthmeier and Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia, both appointed by DeSantis. He has backing from incoming Senate President Jim Boyd and House Speaker Sam Garrison.

Meanwhile, Lieutenant Jay Collins filed a lawsuit to remove Republican candidate James Fishback from the ballot, arguing Fishback fails to meet Florida's constitutional requirement that a governor live in the state for at least seven years before election. Collins' legal complaint cites Fishback's Washington D.C. ties, including claims he designated a D.C. property as his primary residence and voted there in 2020. Fishback denied the allegations and suggested Collins was working with Donalds. The legal battle adds uncertainty to the GOP primary as the August 18 primary date approaches and mail ballots prepare to begin distribution.

cards.headline: Gov. DeSantis moves to designate CAIR and Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist organizations under new Florida law
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis announced Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the Muslim Brotherhood and Antifa as terrorist organizations under a new state law that took effect July 1.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis moved this week to use a new state law that gives Florida a process to designate organizations as terrorist groups. The law, which took effect July 1, allows the governor and Florida Cabinet to designate organizations based on recommendations from state domestic security officials. DeSantis said Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the Muslim Brotherhood and Antifa, along with more than 90 federally designated foreign terrorist organizations, including cartel-linked groups and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

If approved by the Cabinet, the designations could block taxpayer funding, contracts or other public support for listed groups. The law also creates penalties for providing material support and could subject some organizations to dissolution under state statute. CAIR and civil-rights groups quickly sued in federal court, calling the move unconstitutional and warning it could threaten the organization's ability to operate in Florida. Scott McCoy, deputy legal director for the Southern Poverty Law Center, said in a statement that "Gov. DeSantis does not have the power to unilaterally brand an organization with this vilifying designation and punish those who support it without due process or judicial review." The lawsuit argues the designation process violates free-speech and due-process rights.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board challenges judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended for Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended last year for Facebook comments labeling conservative activist Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In its filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone's recommendation contains "numerous findings" that "are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contended that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

In her order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated First Amendment rights. The judge recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. After the judge's recommendation, Theobald told WPTV the case raises questions about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald gets his job back, with no date set for a final decision.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation to nearly double boat slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will shut down July 6 for a major renovation expected to wrap up by next Fourth of July. The $3 million project will significantly expand the facility's capacity, increasing available slips from 18 to 44 for both motorized and non-motorized boats. Funding comes from a state grant and transportation impact fees. The work includes constructing a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform.

The upgrade addresses multiple needs for the city and its boating community. More than 1,400 boaters rely on the dock annually. Beyond simply accommodating more vessels, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed emphasized that the renovation is designed to protect against storm damage during hurricanes and severe weather events. Boat captain Parker Fisher, who operates out of Stuart, supports the improvements. "It's definitely needed some work over the years, so I'm glad they're putting money into it," Fisher said, adding that he hopes the city will consider adding more floating docks to the project.

The city has made efforts to minimize disruption to businesses during the closure. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which depends on the dock for its operations, initially worried about continuing service during construction. However, the city worked with the company to develop a solution. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, explained that the company will be able to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock on the non-floating section to board passengers. Kuyrkendall emphasized the dock's importance to the community, stating that "Stuart is not Stuart without the water."

Kuyrkendall also highlighted the current challenges at the dock, particularly during busy periods. He noted that weekend crowds create congestion, with boats struggling to find available spots. The expansion and modernization of the dock will help ease these pressures. Kuyrkendall said the project represents a positive step forward. "Modernizing and expanding this back dock is really going to be great for the city but also for us as well," he said. Mayor Reed expressed confidence that the year-long wait for completion will prove worthwhile given the improvements the project will bring to Stuart's waterfront and economy.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement and were recognized as first-time winners.

Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, stating "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of the community. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.teaser: Colony Condos residents say beachgoers are cutting through their private property at the JB-7 public walkway since the town removed a fence in 2023, and a replacement could cost significant money.

With only bushes now separating the public access path from private land, the problem intensifies during summer months. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said beachgoers park in private spots and push back bushes to cut through with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. She said residents used to confront trespassers directly, but confrontations became rude encounters, leading them to call police instead.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march along the National Mall in Washington on July 4, representing the entire state of Florida in the prestigious parade.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the magnitude of the moment, noting that millions of people will be watching. "It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion," she said. Senior Stephin Restivo emphasized the team's focus on precision, saying "Everybody is going to be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of." Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, stating she has "full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, noting that it "shows how much we've grown." The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those watching from home.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, and her plastic surgeon are criticizing Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield after the insurer denied coverage for breast reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure involving GalaFlex surgical mesh. According to her denial letter, the surgery was considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it is less risky than other options with proven success. She is requesting that insurers review published literature to see recent updates. Despite the denial, Clark underwent reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a way to make it happen. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. In response to Clark's denial, an Anthem spokesperson said the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community rallies for man who lost fiance Misty Dawn White in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after his fiance, Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday following a fire at their Hobe Sound home.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home she shared with her fiancé in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark stating that Misty had passed away in the fire. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing the piano. She said White was always the first to lend a hand and loved kids and people. The timing of White's death compounds the tragedy, as her birthday is July 4 and she passed away just a few days before it. The loss is further compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. Fenn said White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her.

hero.headline: Juno Beach residents want fence replaced at JB-7 beach access as trespassing disputes escalate
hero.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
hero.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach are asking the town to reinstall a fence at the JB-7 public beach access after removing it in 2023 for safety reasons. The missing barrier has left only bushes between the public walkway and the residents' private property, prompting what condo dwellers say is an increase in trespassing and confrontations during busy summer months.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, described the recurring problem. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. "Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day." Hill said the situation has escalated beyond property damage. When residents initially tried to address the issue directly, she said visitors became defensive. "We used to confront them and tell them this is private property, and they would get pretty rude. So, now what we've just been doing is just calling the police, and they've been coming up and confronting them," Hill said. Hill expressed hope that the town would help restore the boundary, saying "We're really hoping that the town will get back on board and just put it back up, so that we can have our landscaping and our private parking."

The issue reached the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where officials acknowledged the town is not legally required to install a fence. However, Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring affordable alternatives. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. The town council agreed to address the fence question during its upcoming budget discussions scheduled for July 15.

Not all beachgoers perceive a significant problem. Michael House, who visits the beach regularly from a nearby public parking lot, said he has not observed the trespassing issues residents describe. "There's plenty of free parking. If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue," House said. "I have never noticed anyone hopping the fence or the shrubs or anything like that." The disagreement highlights the ongoing tension between providing public beach access and protecting residential property rights in the coastal community.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward on Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. According to Samples, the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with the city's growth. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," Samples said.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial interchange is also still in the design phase. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit system proposed to connect West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles to connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The company will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. Supporters said the system could dramatically improve mobility in one of South Florida's fastest-growing areas by connecting the airport to the convention center, nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying about four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. He referenced previous South Florida light rail discussions that carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could potentially come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach could get elevated self-driving transit connecting downtown to airport
cards.teaser: California-based Glydways will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of autonomous vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to the airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles to connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. The company will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, functioning like a "horizontal elevator" that bypasses traffic congestion. The system could cut the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes, with travel times estimated at seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Gettinger said West Palm Beach is uniquely positioned for the system because major transportation hubs already exist close together but are not easily connected for pedestrians or travelers. While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail discussions with estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community rallies for man who lost fiance Misty Dawn White in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.
cards.body:

Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

cards.headline: Delray Beach golf training center delayed 3 months, costs $90,000 after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen's Tee Box virtual golf training center near Delray Beach was delayed three months after contractor problems forced him to hire a second contractor to redo the work.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, said his project was delayed by three months after problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space. Instead of opening on schedule in April, the work ultimately had to be redone. Molen said the issues cost him about $90,000, an estimate that does not include the revenue lost during the delays or the added expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. He said it was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall.

David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, is warning property and business owners to thoroughly vet contractors before hiring them. Allan estimates 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners face major issues with unvetted contractors. He recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have the proper licenses and insurance before any work begins. According to Allan, the most common contractor complaints in Palm Beach County involve roofing, windows and air conditioning work. Despite the setbacks, Molen said he is focused on moving forward and compared it to the game of golf, saying he has to put that bad shot behind him. Tee Box is set for a grand opening on July 17.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denial hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She chose to have a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. After undergoing the mastectomy, Clark's insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for her reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. According to the denial letter, the procedure involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the product's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. Billington has been a vocal critic of insurance denials and recently shared Clark's case to call for policy changes. Last year, after WPTV's "Patient No More" series shared breast cancer patients' stories of denial, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Anthem said it regularly reviews coverage policies based on medical evidence and that the mesh does not meet standards for coverage without FDA approval. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex a little more than a week ago. A new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act.

hero.body:

According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets relief after lien removed and roof fixed
cards.teaser: A Lantana homeowner and disabled retired veteran received relief after a roofing contractor removed a lien and finished unfinished repairs following WPTV's involvement in the case.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. McCoy made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000 but said two holes were left unfinished on the back side of his home. After attempting to contact the company through calls, texts and emails between January 10 and February 5, McCoy said the contractor stopped responding to his requests for repairs.

Letters from Gulfeagle Supply began arriving at McCoy's home warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien on his property. The lien document stated that Gulfeagle Supply furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid for those supplies. After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, who declined to comment on camera, circumstances changed quickly. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, removing the lien from his home. McCoy also learned the contractor would send crews back to fix the two problem areas on his roof, which occurred about an hour later.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances plans for Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie is moving forward with the Midway Road Widening Project and a partial interchange for Florida's Turnpike to accommodate current and future growth in the city.
cards.body:

Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the current entrances and exits to the Turnpike in Port St. Lucie. The interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth anticipated over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety concerns. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. The partial interchange is still in the design phase. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach Celebrates Fourth of July with Fireworks and Pool Party at Country Club

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach Offers Sea Turtle Nesting Season Programs Through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Florida advances ban on undocumented students at state colleges as Byron Donalds leads GOP governor's race
hero.body:
Florida's State Board of Education voted this week to advance rules that would prevent undocumented students from enrolling in the state's 28 public colleges and adult education programs, including GED preparation courses. The action follows a separate decision by the state university system's Board of Governors to advance a plan barring undocumented students from Florida's public universities starting in the 2027-28 academic year. Students already enrolled would not be affected by the university proposal.

Supporters of the restrictions contend that taxpayer-funded institutions should prioritize students who are lawfully present in the United States. However, immigrant advocates and students have opposed the rules, arguing they would close educational doors for young people who grew up in Florida and graduated from Florida high schools. Alexander Vallejos, a student Dreamer, said "We're just asking for an opportunity to earn our future through education. Because when Dreamers succeed, Florida succeeds." The restrictions come after Florida previously eliminated in-state tuition rates for many undocumented students, including those protected under DACA.

The education restrictions emerged during a dominant week in Florida's Republican governor's race. Byron Donalds entered the week as the front-runner to succeed term-limited Governor Ron DeSantis. His campaign and affiliated political committee report raising more than 90 million dollars this cycle, including more than 23 million in the second quarter. The campaign recently launched a 20 million dollar statewide advertising buy. Donalds also received endorsements from Attorney General James Uthmeier and Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia, both appointed by DeSantis. He has backing from incoming Senate President Jim Boyd and House Speaker Sam Garrison.

Meanwhile, Lieutenant Jay Collins filed a lawsuit to remove Republican candidate James Fishback from the ballot, arguing Fishback fails to meet Florida's constitutional requirement that a governor live in the state for at least seven years before election. Collins' legal complaint cites Fishback's Washington D.C. ties, including claims he designated a D.C. property as his primary residence and voted there in 2020. Fishback denied the allegations and suggested Collins was working with Donalds. The legal battle adds uncertainty to the GOP primary as the August 18 primary date approaches and mail ballots prepare to begin distribution.

cards.headline: Gov. DeSantis moves to designate CAIR and Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist organizations under new Florida law
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis announced Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the Muslim Brotherhood and Antifa as terrorist organizations under a new state law that took effect July 1.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis moved this week to use a new state law that gives Florida a process to designate organizations as terrorist groups. The law, which took effect July 1, allows the governor and Florida Cabinet to designate organizations based on recommendations from state domestic security officials. DeSantis said Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the Muslim Brotherhood and Antifa, along with more than 90 federally designated foreign terrorist organizations, including cartel-linked groups and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

If approved by the Cabinet, the designations could block taxpayer funding, contracts or other public support for listed groups. The law also creates penalties for providing material support and could subject some organizations to dissolution under state statute. CAIR and civil-rights groups quickly sued in federal court, calling the move unconstitutional and warning it could threaten the organization's ability to operate in Florida. Scott McCoy, deputy legal director for the Southern Poverty Law Center, said in a statement that "Gov. DeSantis does not have the power to unilaterally brand an organization with this vilifying designation and punish those who support it without due process or judicial review." The lawsuit argues the designation process violates free-speech and due-process rights.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field site with housing and museum
cards.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid as the preferred redevelopment plan for the Tropicana Field site and Historic Gas Plant District, proposing 3,600 income-restricted housing units and a permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
cards.body:

The park would be part of 18.5 acres of public park space and would include The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad and a concert lawn. The Woodson would serve as "an anchor and a civic landmark for the Gas Plant District" within Samuel Davis Park along a pedestrian corridor called the Legacy Link.

The plan calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units planned within the Historic Gas Plant District and another 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. Blue Sky Communities, a Florida-based affordable housing developer, is listed as the team's affordable and workforce housing partner. The district would be built in three main phases, each expected to take about five years. Phase 1 would establish cultural and workforce anchors, including the Woodson and a Collaboratorium workforce training center. Phase 3 would complete the district with the Resilience Event Center, a Discovery Center Museum and the St. Pete Surf Wave attraction.

The LGBTQ+ Victory Fund endorsed Shevrin Jones for Florida's 24th Congressional District, citing his record of leadership and commitment to the community. cards.headline: Hillsborough County celebrates America's 250th birthday with fireworks and community events across region
cards.teaser: Communities across Hillsborough County are marking America's 250th Independence Day with fireworks, boat parades, drone shows and celebrations from Tampa's downtown waterfront to Plant City.

cards.headline: Americans' pride in U.S. history and democracy drops as country marks 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: A new AP-NORC poll finds Americans have grown less proud of their country's history and the way its democracy works over the past decade, with pride in the armed forces and political influence also declining.
cards.body:
Americans' pride in their country has declined significantly across multiple measures, according to new polling from AP-NORC and Gallup. Americans' pride in the way democracy works has dropped 14 percentage points from 42 percent in February 2017 to 28 percent now. Pride in the armed forces has fallen 19 percentage points since 2017, while pride in U.S. history has declined 14 percentage points. The drops are largely driven by Democrats, with some movement among independents as well. Only 53 percent of U.S. adults say they are extremely or very proud to be an American, the lowest reading in Gallup's trend dating back to 2001.

Partisan divides are stark in these measures. Only 14 percent of Democrats and 28 percent of independents say they are extremely proud to be an American, compared with 70 percent of Republicans. Age also matters: about three-quarters of Americans ages 60 and older say being an American is highly important to their personal identity, compared with only about one-third of U.S. adults under 30. The AP-NORC survey found that 73 percent of Black Americans say their race or ethnicity is extremely or very important to how they see themselves, higher than the share that say that about being an American.

Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on the marching and timing of everything, knowing everyone will see what the Boca High band is capable of. cards.teaser: A recently diagnosed breast cancer patient and her surgeon are criticizing an insurance company that denied coverage for reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before the scheduled procedure.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction planned. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product gives patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. While GalaFlex is popular among plastic surgeons and approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and is still considered an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA reiterated its stance that the treatment's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined." Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. An Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield spokesperson said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they're based on medical evidence and aligned with the latest treatment standards, but the mesh does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by their medical policy. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial, and a new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health & Cancer Rights Act.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach is celebrating a major national honor after being named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. Riviera Beach was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement and were announced as a first-time winner.

Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie approves land transfer for new Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
hero.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of city land to the Florida Department of Transportation. The land will support construction of a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike near Midway Road. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the interchange is designed to improve accessibility and help the city manage growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years. The city council will vote on final approval at an upcoming meeting.

FDOT is currently constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to reduce congestion and improve safety in the area. The first phase of construction involves widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, which will widen the road from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. In addition to the road widening work, FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and designing the partial interchange, which has not yet moved into construction.

Samples explained that Port St. Lucie currently has a significant gap between entrances and exits to the Turnpike. The new interchange will address this gap and help the city accommodate both existing growth and future development. The Midway Road Widening Project will also include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks to improve safety and accessibility for all users.

While residents acknowledge that the ongoing construction in the area can be disruptive, many support the improvements. Erin Scheumeister, a Port St. Lucie resident, said that while the construction work is annoying, she believes the expansion is necessary. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," Scheumeister said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." Her perspective reflects a broader acceptance among community members that the short-term inconvenience of construction is worthwhile to support long-term regional growth and improved transportation infrastructure.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two people wearing life jackets were pulled from the water Wednesday after their small motorized boat became submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man after deadly home fire kills fiancee
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Friends launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many belongings.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn reflected on White's memory, describing her as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand," Fenn said. cards.headline: Martin County School Board challenges judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, claiming "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, which labeled him as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald returns to his position, with no timeline yet announced for a decision.

Senior Jack Williams explained the strategy: "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. Senior Jack Whelche said going undefeated matters less than playoff performance: "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters."

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band earned a spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade and will represent the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
While most people will be relaxing this holiday weekend, the Boca Raton Community High School band will march down one of America's most famous streets. The band earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the magnitude of the opportunity, noting there are millions, if not billions, of people watching. She explained that most people underestimate how physically demanding marching band is. "You have to play, you have to breathe, you have to walk," Cabezas said. "Most people don't realize how difficult it is to walk and maintain that consistent sound without hearing the steps in your music." Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is laser-focused on nailing every detail. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed full confidence in her students to represent the country well. Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, saying it shows how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those watching from home.
